Dear Jeff,

I want to say thank you so much for speaking at our 2001 Deer Valley Conference. I know how difficult making, and then keeping, commitments like this can be. You are a great great friend to have taken the time to help us out. Hopefully it was helpful to you as well. I thought this year's conference was the best ever and the feedback we have already received supports that. We had a fascinating mix of guests and panels and thanks to you it was a smash hit. Deer Valley is our premier client event and you are a premier client. Thank you for being generous with your time. On behalf of all my partners, we appreciate your friendship.

With kind personal regards,

Sincerely,

Jimmy

Hi Jeff,

First, thank you so much for your hospitality the other evening. And good company.

I emailed Jane and she will get the message Monday morning. I put you on the message as well so now you have her address. When I see her I will fill her in on details and mention your willingness to be an active parent when Kristen comes here.

I will also email Brenda Bouchard at the Harvard Club. If you are still interested.

So I checked out enron. You didn't say you were the *largest* energy trading company! Or even say it was a large energy company. Just gas or oil too? Does the name Charles Lawrence mean anything to you? Wall Street. Oil specialty. Checking out your history skills.

Let me know if there is anything more I can do at BU, and let us know when you are coming to Boston again. Maria and Cheryl are very wired into the Hill scene. Maria at the Union Club and Governor's office and Chery everywhere in Boston. And Jane (who you will meet) in the Bahamas.

Regards,

Kay

Jeff:

This is to follow up on my conversation with you last November. At that time I had indicated an interest in moving from GTB in Bolivia to other job within Enron where I can utilize my experience more effectively. You advised me to talk to Jeff McMahon at EIM because you felt my background fits well in his organization. Since than I have been trying to close a number of critical items at GTB. I am happy to report great progress. I talked to Jeff regarding my interest in EIM on Monday. He has indicated a strong interest in me. I am looking forward to hearing from him soon. I would appreciate your support in this. I agree with you that EIM is a great fit for my experience. I really feel I can contribute significantly in Jeff's efforts in expanding markets in Europe.

Regards,

Nasim Khan

Dear Jeff,

Several weeks ago I sent you the draft of a chapter on you in my forthcoming book on great problem solvers. By sending you a courtesy copy in advance of publication, I wanted to give you a chance to help correct or update the text and give me any comments to make sure I'm treating the subject fairly in your mind. My deadline is approaching, but I still haven't heard from you or anyone in your organization. Could you please let me know if you plan to comment, or if there is anything I can do to make the process more convenient. I'm happy to speak to someone on the phone, for instance.

Thanks again for your participation and assistance,

Sincerely,

Christopher Hoenig 202-262-3166

We are pleased to announce the appointment of Carey Sloan as CEO of EnCom and Chairman and CEO of E-Power with immediate effect, reporting to the Office of the Chairman, Enron Europe. He takes over this post from Bruce Wrobel who left the company last month to pursue other interests.

E Power is a wholly owned subsidiary of EnCom Corporation, which in turn is jointly owned by Enron Corp., Japan,s Orix Corp and Yazaki. E Power was created in 1999 to develop independent power plants in Japan.

Carey Sloan joined Enron in 1996, becoming head of business development in Japan and Korea before he joined EnCom/E-Power.

In his new role, Carey will continue to develop greenfield and brownfield power generation opportunities in Japan and will work closely with Enron Japan to maximise the synergies between the two organisations. Enron Japan was officially opened in October 2000 and focuses on multi-commodity merchant business opportunities.

Tatsuro Seguchi will continue in his role of COO of E Power.

Please join us in congratulating Carey on his new appointment.

When he is in town, I set up short meetings for him of 30 minutes or so duration with companies and/or CEO's, Presidents, etc. that he would like to bring industry informaiton to as well as a bit more about us.

I will call after you've had the opportunity to review this to arrange a convenient time for you both.

Michael M. Munn Executive Assistant - Rutherford Consulting -- Overview Presentation.ppt

Jeff, I think Risk can do two things to improve the process: have more of us involved in the process so they actually see the implications of booking deals incorrectly and actively following up on recurring problems. This last one I am particularly bad about. I will see a variance that is rather small and just take it without looking into the underlying cause more carefully. I think the OA group in general should take a more active approach in preventing problems rather than just identifying them. But I know that is easier said than done. DG

My name is Jim Little. I am a forth year Enron employee and a third year student at South Texas College of Law.

I am writing in response to a posting with your group for a Sr. Legal Specialist. The posting itself contains no information about the job other than the fact that it is in the Labor and Employment Department. I realize the expectation may be that I contact the recruiter directly; however, I felt efficiency would be served in contacting you directly. I would appreciate any information you may provide including both duties and necessary qualifications.

I would also appreciate you considering speaking with me in the near future concerning a paper I am writing about individuals with HIV and the protections they are afforded under the ADA. I feel comfortable that Enron has addressed this issue and I am merely guessing that you would have been involved in such discussion or have familiarity through your various writings on the ADA. I am still researching the topic, so it will be a few weeks before I would feel able to ask intelligent questions. But I would appreciate knowing at this time if this is something you are able and willing to discuss.

Thank you for your time,

Jim Little x37703

I know that this is a difficult time for all of us. With everything going on inside the company as well as in the world around us, we have been carefully considering whether a holiday celebration is appropriate this year. To be honest, employee feedback has been mixed. Many viewed the holiday party as a unique opportunity for us to come together as Enron employees to share the spirit of the season. Others felt a holiday party would be improper given the company's current circumstances.

After weighing these points of view, we have ultimately decided to cancel the all-Enron holiday party that was scheduled for December 8. Given what has transpired over the past month, it could be considered imprudent for Enron to incur the expense of such an event. I regret that this action is necessary because I recognize that your hard work throughout the year merits a holiday celebration and so much more. We will attempt to find other, more appropriate ways to recognize your outstanding contributions as we move into the holiday season.

Ken Lay

This is unfortunately not always effective. Hotwire once charged us twice for two hotel rooms for the same person on the same night... in different cities...and with an identical transaction time. Makes no sense and seems impossible ... right? Hotwire wouldn't refund it so we went straight to the credit card company. After a few months we got a letter from VISA saying the charge would stand... because Hotwire had sent in proof that we made both the transactions. They were kind enough to include the "proof" which was simply about 4 photocopied screen shots of the website transaction process, where somebody had typed in our name and address in the form fields, then a bunch of big black arrows drawn on with a marker. It made no sense but VISA bought it.

Hydro Ottawa Thankfully I moved to Toronto where I dont have to deal with this anymore but I had an account with Hydro Ottawa for a year when I lived in an apartment in downtown. I moved back with my parents to pursue an MA and cancelled my account, paying all outstanding fees. They continued to charge me for over a year in random intervals, I kept calling and sending them my bills telling them to stop and they kept saying that my account showed on their system is complete and that they were not debiting my account. It wasn't until my parents and I compared our bills and discovered that the amount I paid was the amount in credit they were receiving and hadn't noticed. They hadn't noticed because they were given a refund for overpaying in the past a few times and it wasn't out of the ordinary. This entire time the Hydro company had put my bank account which is seperate from my parents, to their billing number when I told them that I was moving back home with my parents. They refused a refund and were basically like "aw shucks, sorry" after hours having to speak to one useless CSR after another until the manager finally actually looked into it and realized the error. I will never ever ever give any company, even what is supposed to be a very reputable hydro company my banking information for autodebit every again, this is a scary fuckup, I cant imagine how they handle personal data with other customers.

Turkish Airlines: I booked a flight from Beijing to Istanbul with a domestic connection flight from Harbin to Beijing first. When Harbin-Beijing flight got delayed, i missed my chance to catch my international flight. Guess what! There was no fucking single responsible guy in Turkish Airlines booth who can help me/book a me a new flight. On top of it, in the morning after spending night in airport, I asked for a ticket. Guess what second time! 'We are overbooked. It may take days to get you over Istanbul... unless you pay for a business class ticket.' I had to to go Istanbul. I still can';t believe this fuckers.

Hertz car rental. After they screwed up a simple insurance claim (RV hit my unoccupied, parked rental car, left their insurance info, their insurer denied the claim, Hertz shrugged and said "oh, well-- pay us $$$" instead of pushing it when the other driver was clearly at fault), I staged a one-woman boycott on them for 8 years. Next time I rented with them, they gave my car away less than an hour after my late plane landed-- when all travel was jacked up and delayed due to the new fluids ban. They didn't have another car available, at all-- I was lucky enough to be stranded in a town where I have family to come help me out. After I got home, I wrote them a nasty letter, to which they replied "Too bad." My blog post about their shitty customer service and how to reach an actual human being is still one of the most-found posts in my blog by people searching for "Hertz customer service real address." They hide their address so people can't complain directly.

I have three: Vivint alarm company because my alarm contract auto-renewed for a year a few days before we moved. They said I would have needed to give them at least thirty days notice to cancel. Paid for an alarm system for a year in a house I didn't live in. Landry seafood sold gift certificates to Rainforest Cafe, then closed without notice just a few days after Christmas. I had received a gift certificate and tried to get it replaced for another of their restaurants. They told me to write void on it and mail it to them and they would replace it. They never did. Customer Service never told me I could just use that same certificate at any Landry restaurant. Toys R Us overcharged me and refused to make it right. I had bought two of the same item among a lot of Christmas gift items. I used a coupon for a $10 gift card if I spent a certain amount. At the store I checked my receipt and saw the overcharge, but the way they spread their coupons out, they wanted to refund me less than I paid. They said there was nothing they could do about it (even the manager). It was just a few dollars, but it will cost them hundreds in sales.

Ah greyhound. I was 14 and on a trip with a friend to their cousins house. We got to the station, there were no labels as far as where to stand or anything. A bus pulls up, we ask the driver "Are you going to "location"? He says "yes". Several hours pass. We reach a stop that I realize is very much in the wrong fucking direction. "You said you were going to (location)" "No, we were going to (place we are). Not (location)." Shit shit shit. This was in a ghetto ass section of town at 2 in the morning, we know nobody in the area-fuck, we don't even know the area. We tried to get refunds for our tickets, they said they could only give us a partial refund (nevermind they actually took us FARTHER from where we were trying to go). We had no money on hand except some change-nowhere near enough to cover new tickets. We went to a shit convenience store and used the pay phone outside to call his cousin and let him know what happened. Pissed at greyhounds utter lack of competence or customer service, he decides he will just drive to pick us up (about a 5 hour drive). While waiting, I got bitten by a guard dog, which was one of several that had gotten loose from a construction site nearby that got broken into and robbed. The guy in the convenience store saw what was happening and let us in (they were doing window service only since it was late) helped clean up the dog bite, and let us use his cellphone to call my friends cousin so we wouldn't need to wait outside by the pay phone when he got close.

Ryanair is disgusting. I used to use them because my ex lived in Sweden and it was the cheapest way to get there (I was a poor student), I had items confiscated for being over the liquid limit when they weren't, was told I could have the bottle back if I went to the pharmacy on the airport and bought a 100ml bottle from there, did so, went back and they denyed all knowledge. £20 bottle of L'Occitaine shower gel gone. Was so vexed. They also made me pay an extra £5 charge at the gate for having a bottle of water (which I paid for at the airport) in my carry on luggage. Thankfully they have given me an excuse not to use them any more, they ceased flights from Liverpool John Lennon to Stockholm Skavsta, so I just fly Norweigian Air now, who amusingly aren't much better in the CS side of things, but at least thier planes don't feel like they're from the 1960s.

They are consistently the WORST. For example, my friend was taking an SAT Subject Test, and for some reason the proctor gave them a ton of extra time, like 20 extra minutes (these tests are only an hour). My friend has a lot of integrity and cares a lot about fairness, and it was clear to her that this extra time totally undermined the value of the STANDARDIZED test. So she reports it to the appropriate hotline, hoping at least to prevent this happening again. CollegeBoard gets back to her and informs her that there is not enough evidence to prove misconduct. Therefore there are no repercussions for the proctor or the other students. However, there WAS enough evidence to prove misconduct ON HER PART, so they cancel HER scores.

Rockmount Ranch Wear. Two years ago, we ordered a couple of shirts for my father, but never received them. It was decided that the sales rep, who took the order over the phone wrote down our address and her "7" looked like a "1". The package was shipped to 5401 instead of 5407. The people living in 5401 took the package to the local UPS store to have it returned, but it wasn't seen or heard from again. We learned this several weeks later. During the whole ordeal, we ordered two additional shirts, but Rockmount refused to refund us the money from the first two. And when I say Rockmount, I'm saying the owner, because that's who we were dealing with at this point. He admitted that the shirts were shipped to the wrong address but they wouldn't refund the money until they were returned. He also blamed us stating that it was our fault because we weren't friendlier with the residents four doors down. Long story short, we contested the charge with our credit card company and eventually were credited the money from the first purchase.

Papa Johns - The pizza is horrible but you can order online and they deliver to my office. I stopped using them because of their decision to cut back on Fry and his brethren's hours to avoid providing health benefits. I have since found they have many other despicable practices. At one point in my life I delivered pizzas so I know how hard the job is and what it does to your car. I'm not a socialist or a fiscal liberal but dammed if I am going to support this corporation. I use locally owned pizzerias now. I don't mind ordering by phone and the pizza is better.

Nobody in Best Buy is on commission, As someone who works on commission selling cars let me tell you something. I know very little about the cars themselves, just enough to get by in conversation. However I know an awful lot about how to tell you about This Great Protection Package We Offer in such a way that you won't mind the extra $1500 being added into your deal. I sell new cars so the money I get from selling "products" will pretty much always beat out what I actually make on the car. To give you some perspective the lowest margin vehicle on our lot has less than $300 mark-up (that I get paid on at least) while the average is about $2200. However since pretty much everyone knows "you don't pay MSRP" it's pretty much impossible to actually capture any of that $2200.

Second this. Moved to a different state so I cancelled my service. Called customer service to see where I could drop off my cable box, they have me a specific location in Sacramento. Proceeded to drop it off at the place where they told me to, got a receipt. Comcast called me and said they never received their equipment. Eventually got sent to collections after ten angry phone calls and them saying that I "could fax them the receipt, but it wouldn't matter because they didn't receive their product" from the drop off center they recommended to me.

Zumies. I had recently bought a board from there and went back to get the rest. At first everything was going fine. My friend, his little brother, and I were talking to the semi attractive chick putting it together, talking about how she was a manager, how she has wronged people before because she had a bad day and was annoyed, and had put boards together everyday since she has worked there. An hour and a half later she striped two bolts, put them back to sell to someone else later, and got her brother along with another 'manager' to help put my board together. This fiasco should have taken 15 minutes tops. They lost my business and no sorries were exchanged. Booboo on my heart.

I'm surprised that no one has mentioned Apple yet. Seriously. My school only allowed Apple computers for middle school and high school and those things are terrible. Double the price for a half-assed computer which breaks every fucking month. I had to replace the hard drive of my laptop 5 times in 4 years and re install the OS countless times (I didn't even drop the damn thing). My friend's macbook pro actually caught fire and set off the smoke alarm while he was watching a movie. Their support doesn't even try to figure out what's wrong with your computer and they just opt to backup and wipe everything then copy paste it back. iPhones are also overpriced. I actually had the first iPhone, which didn't even work most of the time. And they come out with a new iPhone every other month, which actually is the same phone but with a slightly better camera. Suprisingly the iPads are the best tablets out right now, that is until android catches up.

Your comment reads like something from /r/circlejerk

Don't be worried about all of the water being owned by greedy corporations. Thirsty people will drink. Most water is used by industry, and there needs to be a way to charge industry for the value added by the water they use.

In some situations, privatization is recommended by the World Bank. In other situations, public ownership of water is recommended. Normally, public municipal water supplies where the bureaucracy is very corrupt actually cause more problems for citizens than privatization will. Sometimes, taking the recommended course doesn't work as intended...usually you can blame it on corruption.

One star off is for a kind-of-hard to follow storyline and certain musical/song choices that are more lulling than fitting. But other than that...

As many reviewers have said before me - all seats are good. Round stage, round auditorium, every seat can see all the action as they have three main stage 'entrances' that are all used in major story transitions. The tickets are also very decently priced compared to other big time Vegas shows like "O", "Love", etc. The performers are A-mazing in terms of their athletic prowess, fit bodies, and aerobic skills. The girls performing with their heads underwater for minutes at a time...major props.

Very beautiful stage, setting, lighting. Could have used more special effects for the "coolness" factor (esp. fire), but no major complaints there. Recommended!

First major show in Vegas, half off due to being a half marathon participant, I was excited (and tired) to see the show! My co-workers and I gathered, got some drinks, admired the circular stage, laughed at the creature from the blue lagoon spitting water at folks in the front row, and then became very bewildered from there...

The story line is a bit unfocused and hard to follow, never quite sure how the different actors/pieces fit into what was originally introduced as the girl's indecision to share her life with the boy or not....

Some neat acts of strength, nice use of the stage and water arena, but all in all, this show just didn't impress me. I think I was just expecting so much more from a Vegas show and had higher hopes than what was presented. Again, a clear understanding of the storyline would've helped as well.

Verdict: Interesting show. For a deeper discount, I'd consider going back, but even at half price, I'm not sure I'd be willing to watch it again or bring anyone that hasn't been there before. Ah well.

P.S. This is not a Cirque du Soleil show, despite what many Yelpers have written. It may have been in the past, but as of December when I visited, it definitely is not advertised as such...

Having been dragged to vegas pre-21, I've had the privilege of watching a lot of the shows in vegas. I have to say this one was not all that impressive compared to others.

The things I did like were; 1. The circular stage. I thought it was nice that anywhere you sit, you get a good view of the show. 2. If you stay at the Wynn or Encore they give you the $125 tickets for the $99 price. 3. Some of the acts were pretty cool. Some of these performers have to be so incredibly strong to do what they are doing and it's impressive (although u can see similar things at cirque de soliel shows)

Things I didn't care for: 1. The story was really bad. Basically there was no story. It was really difficult to follow and it let me wondering half the time, what are they trying to tell us? 2. Besides some impressive stunts, the overall show was only blah. I didn't leave there thinking WOW that was AMAZING! Sometimes I thought there was too much going on and would of been better if they did less. I think whoever put this together got too caught up with the concept of... this is vegas so the show better be big and glittys and more is better. (sometimes less is better!!)

Overall I probably wouldn't go back to see this show again. I don't think it's worth the money a second time. If you haven't seen it though, it might be worth checking out. I did have a few friends that did enjoy the show but I dont' think anyone was blown away by it.

Le Reve was an okay show, but the decor itself is breathtaking from beginning to end. I agree with Misti Y--I think there are those will love Cirque shows and not this show, but that's a whole other talk post.

Breathtaking scenery but a story line that isn't that entertaining is what this show is made of, in my opinion. The stage actually had malfunctions the night I went, so it wasn't easy to stay into the show when things broke down all night long. Although the idea is beautiful, it didn't carry over into real life well.

Despite it's lack of true flair that it strives to steal from the Cirque shows, it's a nice try and something you may want to see just to see the beautiful theater, otherwise you may want to use that money toward another show.

This was my first show in Vegas. After reading the reviews here I had high hopes that it would be better than Cirque, but less expensive. Unfortunately, I came away disappointed.

Granted, the costumes were beautiful. The performers were beautiful. And the set changes will have you scratching your head trying to figure out how they did it. But there's only so much acrobatics that can be done given that there's a large pool of water below and the performers are all wet. Being dropped into the water from 80 feet up is about as complicated as it got.

The first hour of the show was ok, but toward the end the music got monotonous and the performers were dancing more than doing acrobatics. I began to nod off.

I'd like to see a Cirque show some day, but I'm a bit concerned now. If this was *better* than Cirque, and I thought it was merely OK, what will I think of a real Cirque show?

We had planned on seeing "O" when were in Vegas but I think they were on vacation or something. So we decided to give La Reve a shot since it is basically a knock off of O.

We were already staying at Encore so it was a short walk to the theater. We had great seats, 3rd row or so. I think the show has some sort of story, but I had no idea what it was. But that doesn't detract from the enjoyment. Before the show there is a little entertainment in the form of a lizard-like guy that swims around the pool and messes with people in the front rows. At first I thought he was a statue because he'll stay there motionless for a while at times. Then he will sneak up on some unsuspecting theater patron and squirt water at them or something. Pretty funny.

The show is pretty amazing. The pool has platforms in it that raise and lower throughout the show so at times the performers are swimming, diving into the pool or even seemingly walking on water. At one point the performers were diving into the pool from about 25 feet above the water!

So if you want to see a great show and you don't want to pay the astronomical prices for a Cirque de Soleil show, give La Reve a shot.

This is a magical experience which chronicles the story of a lost love. The lighting effects, recurring water theme, music, imagery, and performances all blend together to create an awe inspiring experience. In the beginning the main character finds and loses love abruptly. The story evolves from there with many twists and turns. My capitivation is held by each scene which includes a combination of actors, dancers, synchronized swimmers, and acrobats. Each performance is executed with precision. There are flips and dives into the water, synchronized water perfomances that require performers to hold their breath for many seconds over and over, drama and comedy. All combined to elevate wonder and amazement. It's a must see!

Performance: 4 stars Seat/View: 4 stars

This was our second time seeing this show and we found out that they have changed the costumes and arrangement. I would say there were some pros and cons. Wynn gave us free tickets for the show and we sat at the middle section this time. We could see the overhead lighting better. However, we preferred to sit in the front rows like last time because we had better view of the performers. Also I didn't like they added some dancers around the main characters in some scenes because they created distractions and blocked my sight. Overall it was still a good show and we enjoyed it, especially it was free.

Even though Le R\u00eave means The Dream, the show is so stunning and riveting that no can can sleep through it. Some may compare it to Cirque du Soleil's O - the two shows do have in common water, amazing acrobatics, music and creator Franco Dragone - but any further comparison does disservice to both shows; each is very distinct and unique. Go see it! See it again! And be amazed at the acrobatics, the sets, the lighting, the water, the entire experience. And also see O. Better spend your money on this show than on a boring slot machine or on a blackjack table - you really will not be able to count cards. And you'll save money.

When it comes to Vegas shows I really don't think you can do much better (and I live here so I see lots of shows).

As mentioned below there is no bad seat, and the lower seats may get splashed. I believe the tickets are pricy but as a local I've never paid full price. I recently got a backstage tour with a friend who knows one of the performers and you wouldn't believe the inner workings of this thing. I'm surprised I don't hear about accidents regularly so they must run a tight ship.

As most know the show is a dream sequence. However, if you are like me and are not artistic or good at understanding abstract art pieces, you'll never know what's going on. On the other hand, there are so many performers and there is so much going on all over the theater, its still entertaining to those of us who don't "get" it.

Its definately worth the time and money.

My unbiased rating is 4 stars but my biased rating would be somewhere around 2.5-3 stars.

I've never been interested in watching a cirque de soleil show and this is my first one. It had a lot less backflips and crazy acrobatics then i expected....much more interpretive dancing type stuff. Either way the stuff these guys and gals do are very impressive and i'm sure anyone that is a fan of these types of shows would enjoy Le Reve.

Personally i would never pay the 100+ dollars to watch these shows but we got free tickets so yay!

There's no bad seats in this venue, but we got VIP seating for the chocolates and champagne..lol and there is a private monitor to view behind the stage/underwater chaos that takes place during the show. Ushers and hostess were awesome. We had a loud couple next to us and the usher offered to move us if it wasn't tolerable. This was the good.

The bad. I'm not a big fan of cirque productions, so I can't say I enjoyed it. It's typical though, if you like that kind of show. I've seen Mystere and Ka also and I would rate those the same. Impressive stuff though.

We came here on a Friday about 4:30pm and there was no line!! I paid around $130.00 for 2 people because I figured it would be the same price as a steakhouse. (I found out later that the buffett was a bit more) If you are looking for steak you will disappointed like I was. I assumed that steak would be an option because of the pricing of the buffett but I was wrong. They had other choices like lamb, prime rib and chicken. You can get most of these choices at other buffets for much cheaper.

I skipped over to the seafood which had Alaskan crab legs and rock crab claws. The Alaskan crab legs you can get at most Las Vegad buffets but the rock crab claws I haven't seen. The reason why I was dissatisfied is because they don't have crab claw crackers. I was told they had wooden mallots but I didn't want to go in that direction because we were seated too close to the other table. I didn't want to have crab shells flying all over the place so I just had the crab legs.

I checked out the Asian station but I didn't find anything special. It was comparable to the Rampart Casino Buffett ( which isn't saying much). The dessert bar had no real stand out items for me. They had gelato and an assortment of pastries. They do have fresh juices though but I didn't try any of them.

It is a good buffet but it is overpriced for what it is. If you must try it to see for yourself then you should go but if there is a long line I would think twice.

I have no idea how this buffet tastes because their system is awful. We showed up at 7:20 on a Sunday night to have time for a 10:00pm show at the same hotel. We had to put our name in a digitized system to come back and pay at 8:23 - the system absolutely was pointless. We waited until 8:40 to be told we wouldn't be seated until 9:15 most likely, and for a party of two there was nothing they could do. If they had said the wait would be an hour longer than our time to pay we wouldn't have wasted our time, but we ended up instead with a very irritating experience. 0 stars if it was possible for this.

Beware - gnats abound in this buffet. The presentation was unbelievable but when we settled in for desert the gnats attacked. Having spent over $100 for dinner for 2 I asked for a manager. This goon named Wolf came and said this has been a problem before but since we were onto desert there was nothing he would do for us. I contacted customer service after arriving home and while they were sympathetic all that was offered was a return visit. Since I was 2500 miles away I asked for something comparable in one of their locations closer to home and was ignored. No reply at all. Needless to say I will not be returning there or any of their other locations. Follow up - It took contacting their corporate office several times but eventually they did the right thing and gave me a full refund.
